entries.review_reason: Replaced the while-downloading converb with an explicit request-message topic/object. The request content names downloading the Commons file; the matrix send predicate acts on itak, not cinuyep. Again plus a different original-file URL describes redirection. It is a failure report, not a user retry instruction.
grammar_analysis: cinuyep is the explicit object of transitive a=ranke; rusuy scopes over that verb.
sekor a=ye licenses the content clause. Its following head itak denotes the message saying that content.
anak topicalizes the whole request-message; a=eikra has this overt object. The file noun inside the subordinate content clause is not the matrix object.
mosma hoski cinuyep kor URL or un is the new destination; suy modifies send to express the follow-on request. The implementation opens a new connection after a Location response.

entries.transliteration: Commons ci bithe be alime gaire be baire gisun be, gūwa da bithe i URL de guribuhe.
entries.nonblocking_uncertainty: Source-assisted compositional language review; neither native-speaker certification nor a universally standardized modern technical vocabulary is claimed. Application/device layout and complete build remain separate gates.
entries.back_translation: [They] transferred the message requesting receipt of the file from Commons to the URL of a different original file.
entries.review_reason: Replaced the receiving converb with a nested receiving-request clause headed by gisun, explicitly accusative-marked by the final be. The transferred object is the download request. Including alime gaire in the request content prevents the wording from collapsing into an ambiguous file search. guribuhe reports the completed redirection, and the destination is another original-file URL.
grammar_analysis: Commons ci marks the provider source. bithe be is the inner object of alime gaire.
alime gaire be is an accusative-marked participial event, the object of baire; Gorelova p500 licenses this nested complement structure.
baire modifies gisun. The outer gisun be is the matrix direct object of guribuhe, so neither a hidden downloading actor nor the file is what moves.
gūwa da bithe i URL de names a different original-file URL as destination.
gaire and baire are verified irregular participial forms; guribuhe is independently attested in a primary-document index.
semantic_equivalence: Receiving a file from Commons identifies the download.
Request-message is the explicit redirected object.
Different original file and its URL are retained.
No file-moving/uploading claim or successful-receipt converb remains.
entries.orthography_review: Each Manchu-script token was read against the romanized analysis. One U+202F binds bithe to genitive i in the application’s established encoding. gūwa uses Manchu ū; guri uses u. No Sibe-only substitutions are present.
